10.1002_adfm.77481: Electrocatalysis is central to sustainable energy and environmental remediation, yet its efficiency is fundamentally governed by electron transfer dynamics. While conventional research predominantly relies on the molecular‐level design of active sites, this approach often falls short in overcoming the sluggish electron‐transfer kinetics across complex multi‐phase interfaces. Breaking away from traditional active‐site‐centric paradigms, this review innovatively reframes electrocatalyst design through the lens of micro‐to‐mesoscopic electrode architectures, explicitly targeting the manipulation of electron transfer behaviors. We systematically unveil how strategic interface and spatial engineering, encompassing defect confinement, built‐in electric fields (BIEFs), and structurally tailored zero‐to‐three‐dimensional (0D‐3D) architectures, can steer electron transfer pathways, amplify local electron density, and drastically lower kinetic barriers. By decoding the intricate structure‐activity‐electron transfer relationships, this review establishes a pioneering framework for functionalizing electrode microenvironments. Ultimately, mastering these electron transfer dynamics will pave the way for transcending current performance limits in heterogeneous electrocatalysis, offering transformative solutions for the food‐energy‐water nexus toward a sustainable future.
10.1002_advs.202524109: The lithium plating reaction in graphite electrodes acts as a root cause for the accelerated degradation and the internal short circuits in lithium-ion batteries. Here, an electrochemical model based on multi-scale microstructural images was established to identify lithium plating-stripping processes, thereby supporting the predictive outcomes of electrochemical monitoring techniques. Experiments revealed that the open-circuit voltage differential curve (dOCV/dt) led to ambiguous delineation of the safe state-of-charge (SOC) operating range. The established lithium plating-stripping model was used to compare with experimental results, revealing the dynamic evolution of electrode-scale kinetics and quantified the impact of lithium metal residue on electrode performance. Ex situ X-ray computed tomography (XCT) captured micrometer-resolution microstructural details of graphite electrodes and plated lithium, enabling further correlation of spatially heterogeneous lithium plating-stripping reactions with electrode microstructure. The sensitivity of lithium plating to electrode microstructure was examined at the particle scale, attributed to competition between electrode kinetic rates and active reaction areas. Theoretical mechanism analysis and experimental results from high-energy-density electrodes demonstrated that positioning small particles on the current collector side effectively mitigates solid-state diffusion polarization while confining side reactions to a limited area. The integration of experiments and multiscale modeling elucidates the relationship between lithium plating-stripping reactions and electrode structure, providing mechanistic insights for similar structural optimization designs.
10.1002_anie.1526477: Electrocatalysis is essential for renewable energy conversion, yet the mechanisms governing catalytic performance remain poorly understood due to the complex nature of electrochemical interfaces. Advances in nanomaterial synthesis and high‐resolution characterization now allow detailed structural and compositional analysis, but static methods fall short of capturing the dynamic behaviors of active sites during operation. In this review, we focus on the growing role of in situ and operando techniques such as optical, X‐ray, and electron‐based, in resolving catalytic structure and reactivity under real‐life working conditions. These methods offer unparalleled access to the evolution of surface species, reaction intermediates, and interfacial topologies that govern catalytic functions. We highlight how in situ and operando studies have revealed transient phenomena and mechanistic details previously inaccessible, and discuss their critical roles in advancing systems for water splitting, CO 2 /N 2 reduction, and fuel cells related renewable energy applications. Beyond highlighting the real‐time transformations captured by operando and in situ methods, this review underscores how coupling operando datasets with theoretical modeling and machine learning can accelerate mechanistic discovery and enable rational catalyst design. By extracting hidden correlations and guiding closed‐loop experimentation, data‐driven approaches promise to reduce reliance on empirical trial‐and‐error and unlock predictive control over catalytic performance. Taken together, these developments position operando characterization, when coupled with AI‐driven interpretation, as a cornerstone of future energy research, providing a pathway to accelerate discovery, design, and deployment of next‐generation electrocatalysts.
10.1002_smll.76424: The 1,4‐butanediol oxidation reaction (BDOR) provides a sustainable platform for producing valuable chemicals, yet its reaction kinetics remain constrained by inefficient proton transfer. Inspired by nature's enzymatic proton transfer systems, we report a bioinspired terephthalate‐modified NiFe‐catalyst (NiFe‐TPA) for efficient BDOR in a flow‐cell electrolyzer. Spectroscopic and mechanistic analyses revealed that TPA modification tailored the electronic and coordination environments and enhanced proton transfer kinetics during BDOR. As a result, NiFe‐TPA produced 100 mA cm −2 current density at 1.40 V vs. RHE for BDOR and 1.51 V vs. RHE for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). When integrated into a flow cell, NiFe‐TPA required a cell voltage of 2.1 V, reaching 1 A current for BDOR‐assisted water electrolysis. Electrochemical analysis with in situ Raman spectroscopy indicated that NiFe‐TPA involved γ‐Ni(O)OH phase for OER while TPA mediated proton transfer enhancement for BDOR. Our findings establish a broadly applicable design strategy for developing high‐performance bioinspired catalysts for electrocatalytic oxidation reactions.
10.1016_j.apenergy.2026.127553: Due to their superior rapid response capabilities, community energy storage systems (CESS) can readily secure bids for frequency control ancillary services (FCAS). However, insufficient attention has been paid to the constrained integration of CESS and prosumers for FCAS, particularly in terms of ensuring the safe operation of CESS. This paper proposes a coordination framework based on a battery modular energy management model for CESS and prosumers within a community. The battery module's lifespan is considered and extended by regulating the depth-of-discharge range for each module of CESS. Leveraging the capacity rental of CESS can ensure uninterrupted FCAS performance, even in the presence of severe CESS module degradation and substantial frequency deviations. The coordination framework can foster additional arbitrage opportunities for prosumers. The effectiveness of the proposed coordination framework for CESS and prosumers, as well as capacity rental model, is validated through simulations on a modified IEEE 39-bus system in various CESS states. A rolling quota allocation algorithm is proposed to dynamically adjust the participation quotas of residential and industrial prosumers based on their activity levels, thereby establishing a differentiated allocation mechanism that effectively addresses the limitations of traditional static schemes in adapting to changes in prosumer behavior. The simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively mitigate the degradation of CESS and enhance profitability for proactive prosumers and CESS.
10.1016_j.matdes.2026.116611: Retaining electrochemically generated carbide films on reactive metal substrates is limited by the coupling between carbon supply, substrate consumption, and product detachment. Here, Mo electrodes in LiCl-KCl-K 2 CO 3 melts were used to examine how pulse regulation controls retained Mo 2 C film growth during carbonate electroreduction. Although Ni and Mo showed similar cyclic voltammetric responses in the main carbonate-reduction region, phase and microstructural analyses revealed a substrate-dependent pathway on Mo. High current density produced dendritic carbonaceous deposits together with Mo 2 C, whereas low current density suppressed isolated carbon deposition and promoted interfacial Mo 2 C formation. However, prolonged galvanostatic electrolysis continuously consumed the near-surface Mo substrate, generated a porous support region, and caused Mo 2 C detachment. The collected detached products agreed with the calculated Mo2C-equivalent mass, showing that formation was not the limiting step; retention was. Pulse electrolysis resolved this formation-detachment behavior by temporally regulating carbon supply and interfacial reaction. A continuous Mo 2 C layer formed at the early stage and thickened to approximately 35 μm as a surface-retained layer. These results refine the post-carburization view of Mo 2 C growth and identify pulse regulation as a route for retained carbide-film growth during molten-carbonate electroreduction.
10.1021_acsenergylett.5c03342: Oxynitride photocatalysts drive the hydrogen and oxygen evolution reactions under visible light with sacrificial reagents, but overall water splitting remains challenging, pointing to unresolved interfacial energetics. Here we integrate SrTaO 2 N and the (Ba x Sr 1– x )TaO 2 N solid solution into particulate photoelectrodes and quantitatively probe their semiconductor properties at the solid/liquid interface. Beyond the rectifying behavior established for single-crystal photoelectrodes, electrochemical measurements using a reversible Fe 3+ /Fe 2+ redox couple identify a defect-derived surface state located at 0.5 V vs the reversible hydrogen electrode in photocatalysts that mediates irreversible electron transfer. While this state enables half-reactions and rationalizes Z-scheme water splitting with suitable mediators, it promotes carrier recombination and thereby suppresses overall water splitting. This study establishes an electrochemical methodology that bridges photocatalyst powders and interfacial energetics and indicates that eliminating or passivating the defect states should enable overall pure water splitting in oxynitrides.
